column1: # Confirmed-distinct customer families — names that LOOK like duplicates but are not.
# Sibling of reference/customer-aliases.tsv. That file says "these two strings are one
# customer." This one says the opposite: "these strings share words, and we have decided they
# are different customers." Without it, scripts/customer-aliases.py --suggest re-proposes the
# same merges every week, and a proposal list that is mostly noise stops being read.
# Read ONLY by the suggester. It does not affect canonicalization or counting — an unmapped
# name already counts as itself. Recording the decision here changes nothing about the
# numbers; it stops the question being re-asked.
# Format: three TAB-separated columns. Lines starting with # are comments.
#   family label<TAB>name | name | name<TAB>why they are distinct
# Every pair WITHIN a family is suppressed. Pairs across families are still proposed.
# The rule behind these decisions: a customer is a BUYING ACTIVITY — an organization that
# holds its own money and writes its own requirements — not a service or a parent agency.
# Merging separate program offices understates real demand breadth exactly as badly as

column2: U.S. Army | U.S. Army Futures and Concepts Center (FCC/ICED) | Army Contracting Command - APG | Army Contracting Command - DTA | Army Materiel Command (ACC-CTRS)
column3: Five distinct Army buying activities. Bare "U.S. Army" is the enterprise-wide ONIX Marketplace Challenge, not a vague spelling of a command — it is a real Army-wide requirement owner. ACC-APG and ACC-DTA are separate contracting offices under one command and issue separate solicitations.
